s1.syndrome_frame: Exertional chest pain with transient ECG changes
salient_findings: Left bundle-branch block (LBBB) during stress test
key_facts: Patient in their early 60s
2-week history of chest pain during exertion
Chest pain consistently presented during physical activity
Patient is a nonsmoker
No family history of premature coronary artery disease
Baseline 12-lead ECG showed no substantial abnormalities
Stress ECG developed LBBB in stage 2 at heart rate of 107 beats per minute
LBBB resolved following exercise cessation with immediate angina relief
No ischemic or memory T waves in pre- and post-exercise ECGs
Coronary computed tomography angiography showed no abnormalities

shortlist.label: Coronary artery spasm
shortlist.why_kept: Exertional chest pain with transient ECG changes and no evidence of coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Prinzmetal's angina
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain during exertion and transient ECG changes are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Myocardial bridge
shortlist.why_kept: Exertional chest pain and transient ECG changes could be related to a myocardial bridge

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy can cause exertional chest pain and ECG changes

shortlist.label: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease
shortlist.why_kept: Despite normal coronary computed tomography angiography, this diagnosis cannot be entirely ruled out due to the patient's age and exertional chest pain

raw.rationale: The patient's chest pain during exertion, development of LBBB during stress ECG that resolved with exercise cessation, and immediate angina relief without evidence of ischemic changes or coronary artery disease on computed tomography angiography, are consistent with coronary artery spasm.

rejected.label: Prinzmetal's angina
rejected.why: While similar, Prinzmetal's angina typically occurs at rest and is associated with transient ST-segment elevation, which was not observed in this case.

rejected.label: Myocardial bridge
rejected.why: Myocardial bridge could cause exertional chest pain, but the absence of specific findings like systolic compression of the coronary artery on imaging makes it less likely.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There's no mention of left ventricular hypertrophy or other characteristic features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in the provided information.

rejected.label: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease
rejected.why: The coronary computed tomography angiography showed no abnormalities, making atherosclerotic coronary artery disease less likely as the cause of the patient's symptoms.
